summary: Cross-vendor adversarial panel over the intent-to-completion spec-gate artifacts (spec.md rev 13 + goals.md), bytes embedded verbatim

result.summary: Two blockers survive in-tree verification of spec rev 13. (1) `push_archive` (spec.md:495) is a new unconditional default in the core finish order for every repo that adopts v10, fires with no AUQ under `loose`, is missing from the §4.2 always-halt list (spec.md:165) that fleet policy would put it in, has no config opt-out (§4.1 has no such key), and its "fast-forward by construction" premise assumes a `done.install` push that does not exist for the ~40 sibling repos on this host that carry masterplan bundles and no `.masterplan.yaml` at all (verified by scan) — v9 today pushes only after the operator picks `pr` at the always-halting `branch_finish` AUQ (lib/finish-step.mjs:316-320, commands/masterplan.md:243,249), so this is genuinely new unreviewed network publication, and on the masterplan repo itself GitHub `main` is the Claude marketplace production surface. (2) The rev-13 S6 fix for `high` critic cadence is gameable as written: §4.2/§5.4 require only "a critic receipt recorded after each intent round's last content event" (spec.md:143, 326), `mp interview ask` (spec.md:254) never refuses opening round r+1 without a receipt for round r, so four back-to-back rounds plus one trailing receipt satisfy `converged` with one critic pass, and the §11 test is worded with the same "following receipt" predicate so it would certify the bypass — this undermines Outcome 1/G1, the run's primary goal. Six should-fixes follow (an operator-gated but §7.1-contradicting `deploy_indeterminate` "mark done with evidence" path into `complete`; `git patch-id --stable` whitespace-blindness reproduced on this host with two semantically different Python diffs sharing one id while `--verbatim` distinguishes them; ask+withdraw padding rounds counting toward the intent-round minimum; a sibling-repo scan rooted at `<MAIN>/../*` = `/srv/dev/ras/*` that misses `/srv/dev/*/`, `/srv/dev/*/*/` and `/srv/workflows` (two in-progress bundles verified) while the AUQ implies the list is exhaustive; a `required-successor` check that is WARN-forever when absent and binds slug+completion rather than the `--predecessor` relationship; and a step-5 push that carries local `main`'s non-bundle commits — 20 ahead, 3 non-bundle right now — into the tag and production `main` without naming them at `publish_ack`). Five nits and seven dropped claims are itemized. Verdict: revise.

findings.claim: `push_archive` is an unconditional new default in the v10 finish order for every repo, fires with no AUQ under `loose`, has no opt-out, is omitted from the always-halt gate list, and its fast-forward/only-new-history premise is false for repos with no `done:` block or `done: none`.
findings.failure: Any repo with autonomy `loose` and no `.masterplan.yaml` (verified: every sibling repo on this host with masterplan bundles — /srv/dev/ehr, /srv/dev/petabit/*, /srv/dev/yanos-project/*, /srv/workflows, 40+ total — has none) runs an ordinary `merge` finish → `no_definition_of_done` gate → archive incomplete → `push_archive` executes `git push origin main` directly, publishing every local-only commit on `main` (WIP, unreviewed, unrelated to the run) to origin with no gate; on the masterplan repo origin `main` is the Claude marketplace production surface. Second leg (reviewer 1): with a multi-host unprotected origin the push can be rejected non-fast-forward after the bundle is already locally archived `complete`, and §7.2 defines no fetch/rebase/re-target disposition — re-entry only re-emits the same rejected push; `archive_pushed` is written after the push so it is never part of the pushed history and peers will re-emit the op.
findings.location: docs/masterplan/intent-to-completion/spec.md:495 (§7.2 push_archive row); spec.md:165 (§4.2 always-halt list); §4.1 config table (no push_archive key); A34 spec.md:1307. Precedent: lib/finish-step.mjs:316-320, commands/masterplan.md:243,249 (v9 pushes only after the branch_finish AUQ).
findings.fix_direction: Add `push_archive` to the §4.2 always-halt list (an AUQ at every autonomy level, matching fleet policy that push is a risky-action gate) and/or scope it to fire only when a `done.install` group actually pushed the base; add a config-plane key (`push_archive: on|off`, default off when `done` is absent or `none`); define a non-fast-forward disposition (fetch, per-commit audit of the foreign range, rebase the archive commit, retry) and state that local `complete` is not durable until `archive_pushed` lands.

findings.claim: The `high`-complexity 'critic after every intent round' requirement is enforced only by an event-log-position predicate ('a receipt recorded after that round's last content event'), so one trailing critic receipt satisfies every earlier round, and the §11 test is worded to certify the bypass.
findings.failure: At `high`: record four intent rounds back-to-back (nothing in the `mp interview ask` refusal list at spec.md:254 — duplicate id, out-of-sequence id, non-current/next round, sealed round, unanswered earlier round, past cap — blocks opening round r+1 without a critic receipt for round r); record a draft; dispatch the critic once with a clean payload; `mp interview end --reason=converged` succeeds because that single receipt's ledger index is later than rounds 1–3's last content events too. §4.2 (spec.md:143) says this is 'enforced, not advisory' and that four rounds mean 'at least four critic passes'; the §11 case 'converged refused while any intent round lacks a following critic receipt' passes on the bypass. Outcome 1 / G1 is the run's primary goal.
findings.location: docs/masterplan/intent-to-completion/spec.md:143 (§4.2), :254 (§5.3 ask refusals), :326 (§5.4 converged row 'at high' clause), §11 interview-ledger-resume additions
findings.fix_direction: Require a distinct receipt per intent round: either `ask` refuses to open intent round r+1 while round r (sealed) has no critic receipt whose `content_head` falls at or after round r's last content event and before round r+1's first ask, or `converged` requires count(distinct receipts with non-overlapping content_head coverage) ≥ completed intent rounds. Reword the §11 test to assert that one trailing receipt is refused for four rounds.

findings.claim: The `deploy_indeterminate` gate's 'mark done with evidence' resolution records a `deploy_step` for a mandatory `live_check` step without any check predicate having exited 0, contradicting §7.1's 'a declared step that did not happen cannot be talked into the ledger' and Outcome 3's 'the live check passed'.
findings.failure: A `live_check` step whose `check` exits 2 (or a step with no `check`, as in the §7.1 sample's live_check group) reaches `deploy_indeterminate`; the operator selects 'mark done with evidence' with any digest-bearing file; `deploy_step` is recorded, `goals_unmet` (final) is waived, `intent_confirm` is answered, and the bundle archives `completion: complete` with no live-check predicate ever having passed. Operator-gated and durable, so not silent — but the completion class is wrong and the §7.1 invariant is false as stated.
findings.location: docs/masterplan/intent-to-completion/spec.md:488 (§7.2 deploy_indeterminate row); §7.1 'Free-text evidence is never accepted as proof'; Outcome 3
findings.fix_direction: For `live_check` (and any mandatory step lacking `check`), remove 'mark done with evidence' or make it record `deploy_step {status: attested}` that yields archive class `incomplete:attested`, never `complete`; a step with `check` may only be closed by a subsequent `check` exit 0.

findings.claim: The `pr` squash proof via `git patch-id --stable` ignores whitespace, so a squash whose indentation differs from the reviewed branch — semantically significant in Python/YAML/Makefiles — is accepted as equivalent.
findings.failure: Reproduced on this host (git 2.53.0): branch b1 moves `b = 2` inside an `if` block; branch b2 dedents it to 2 spaces outside the block; `git diff X^ X | git patch-id --stable` yields the identical id 76f36b5e… for both, while `git patch-id --verbatim` yields distinct ids. Under §7.3 finish accepts the squash, deploys it, and archives `complete` on code that behaves differently from what was reviewed.
findings.fix_direction: Use `git patch-id --verbatim` (available since git 2.39), or compare the squash's resulting tree against the branch's tree applied on the same base (`git diff --stat <squash> <branch_tip>` empty modulo the merge base), and add a whitespace-only-difference fixture to `deploy-commit-identity`.

findings.claim: A round counts as 'completed' toward the intent-round minimum when every question is answered OR withdrawn, so ask-and-immediately-withdraw rounds pad the minimum with zero operator content, and each withdraw advances `content_head`, compounding the per-round critic bypass.
findings.failure: At `high` after one genuine answered round meeting the floors, ask one intent question in each of rounds 2–4 and withdraw it immediately; four 'completed' intent rounds exist with answers only in round 1, satisfying §5.4's round-minimum gate; the withdraws move `content_head` so one trailing receipt covers them.
findings.location: docs/masterplan/intent-to-completion/spec.md:137 (§4.2 intent-round minimum definition); §5.3 content_head includes intent withdraws; §5.4
findings.fix_direction: A completed intent round must contain at least one answered intent-kind question to count toward the minimum; add the padding fixture to `interview-ledger-resume`.

findings.claim: The `install_pi` sibling-repo scan (`<MAIN>/../*/docs/masterplan/*/state.yml`) is not host-wide although the Pi install root is a host-wide singleton, and the step-4/publish_ack AUQs present the list as every in-flight run on the host.
findings.failure: Verified in-tree: MAIN is /srv/dev/ras/masterplan, so the scan reaches only /srv/dev/ras/*; masterplan bundles also exist under /srv/dev/*/ (ehr, yanos-project), /srv/dev/*/*/ (petabit/*, hw/*, openxcvr/*, yanos-project/*, agents/*) and /srv/workflows, which right now carries two `status: in-progress` schema-9 bundles (agent-policy, ultracode-revamp) and is the fleet's hook-policy source. None would be named in the AUQ; `install_pi` swaps their binary anyway.
findings.fix_direction: Scan a configured set of workspace roots (e.g. `/srv/dev` recursively to depth 3 plus `/srv/workflows`, from `--targets` or a fleet inventory such as /srv/dev/llms.txt) rather than parent-directory siblings, and state in the AUQ that the list may be incomplete; call out the hook-policy repo explicitly when it appears.

findings.claim: `required-successor` is soft enforcement: the successor absent yields a permanent non-blocking WARN (exit 0), the check binds by slug and completion class rather than the `--predecessor` relationship, and there is no staleness escalation.
findings.failure: If `v10-validation` is never seeded, CI stays green forever and Outcome 7's 'required, non-deferrable' successor is indistinguishable from 'about to be seeded'. Separately, any run seeded with slug `v10-validation` but without `--predecessor=intent-to-completion` that archives `complete` discharges the obligation without exercising the deploy stage. Panel-3 B1 forced WARN-when-absent because this repo's CI runs the bare doctor on every push and `v*` tag (verified: .github/workflows/ci.yml Doctor step, no `--only`), so the self-referential CI cannot supply teeth.
findings.location: docs/masterplan/intent-to-completion/spec.md:557-570 (§7.4 required_successor / doctor severity table); spec.md:1252 (B1); Outcome 7 spec.md:44-52
findings.fix_direction: Bind the check to a successor whose seed event names `--predecessor=<this slug>` (not slug alone); either state in the Assumptions table that enforcement is soft-only, or add a time-boxed WARN→ERROR promotion (recorded `due_by` on the `required_successor` event) or a host-level sweep outside this repo's push-triggered CI.

findings.claim: Step 5 pushes local `main`'s non-bundle commits — already ancestors of the branch tip and therefore inside the v10 tag and Pi install — to production without those commits ever appearing in a reviewed diff or being named at `publish_ack`.
findings.failure: Verified now: local `main` is 20 commits ahead of origin/main, 3 non-bundle (0b6159d WORKLOG, abc3b0a and 5aa3c27 workflow-map regenerations). The run branch is created from local `main` HEAD (lib/worktree.mjs), so `git diff main...branch_tip` in both the pre-publish and finish-time reviews excludes them; the tag at branch_tip contains them; step 4 publishes the tag and step 5 pushes them to GitHub `main`. The pre-publish verify (full suite at the tip) covers functional breakage, semantic defects are not reviewed. Reviewer 1's claim that A21/A28 are thereby 'false' is not supported — neither assumption asserts review coverage of pre-existing `main` history.
findings.fix_direction: Have `mp bootstrap arm --step=main_push` list every non-bundle commit in `origin/main..main` (sha, subject, paths) and fold the list into the `publish_ack` AUQ text; optionally require an explicit `--carry=<sha,…>` acknowledgement recorded in the `main_push` event.

findings.claim: Frozen G6's 'before this run's finish begins' is literally false on the §10.3 corrective-release path, where v10.0.x is installed after finish began and the finish is re-entered.
findings.failure: Finish begins → blocking review → `mp bootstrap start --pass=2` → v10.0.1 tagged/installed → finish re-entered → G6 assessed at v10.0.1 via command-class liveness evidence, which cannot see the ordering; the verdict is right in spirit and the goal text is imprecise.
findings.fix_direction: `mp goals-amend` G6's temporal phrase to 'before the goal check of the finish attempt that archives this run' (or 'before the finish attempt of record').

findings.claim: `done.commit_paths` is validated only as a path list, so a repo author can allowlist executable paths and re-open the A30 hole; the default also includes the `version_from` file, which a stage step could rewrite after `${version}` was resolved at `deploy_base_sha`.
findings.failure: `commit_paths: [src/]` in a repo's reviewed `.masterplan.yaml` lets a `release` step's generator commit application code that advances the audit base while `completion_confirmed` binds to the pre-stage sha. Requires the author to write the self-defeating config or a version-rewriting step; `release.mjs` itself never bumps.
findings.fix_direction: Warn at seed when an allowlist entry is a directory or a non-metadata file, and add a per-stage-commit postcondition that `${version}` at `base_after` equals the value resolved at `deploy_base_sha`.

findings.claim: §10.1's `record` 'refuses a step whose postcondition fails' is not reconciled with §10.3's requirement that every failed irreversible action leaves a durable `bootstrap_step {status: failed}` (e.g. a partial push whose remote-tag-equality postcondition fails).
findings.failure: Read literally, a failed push can never be recorded (the postcondition fails so `record` refuses), leaving only `bootstrap_armed` on the bundle and no failed record to resume from; read charitably `--status=failed` bypasses the postcondition, but the spec does not say so.
findings.fix_direction: State that `record --status=failed` skips the success postcondition, requires `--exit≠0` or an explicit failure reason, and is the only record accepted after a failed command; the attestation half of reviewer 1's finding is already disclosed as A33.

findings.claim: The gate's claim that the rebase 'cannot conflict because the merged code never touches the bundle directory' is by design but never asserted as a precondition.
findings.failure: If the run branch ever carried a change under `docs/masterplan/<slug>/` (the design says bundle writes go to the base branch, but nothing checks the branch), the state-only audit accepts a later bundle commit on local `main` touching the same file and `git rebase origin/main` conflicts with no disposition.
findings.fix_direction: Add to `arm --step=gate` the precondition `git diff --name-only $(git merge-base main branch_tip) branch_tip` contains no `docs/masterplan/` path (the §10.3 sibling-push row already computes this list).

findings.claim: A one-time v9→v10 bootstrap is implemented as permanent product surface (`lib/bootstrap.mjs`, four `mp bootstrap` subcommands in the flag whitelist and help, a permanent test suite) when the repo already has a one-off `scripts/` pattern.
findings.failure: Every future refactor of finish/bundle schemas must keep `lib/bootstrap.mjs` and `v9-to-v10-bootstrap.test.mjs` consistent for a path that never executes again after `v10-validation`. A33's rationale (preconditions in code, surviving compaction) is satisfied equally by a `scripts/bootstrap-v10.mjs` importing `lib/` and the single event writer.
findings.location: docs/masterplan/intent-to-completion/spec.md:711-750 (§10.1 driver), §12 touch surface, A33 spec.md:1306; scripts/v5-orphan-grep.sh (existing one-off pattern)
findings.fix_direction: House the driver under `scripts/` (importing the event writer and schema validator from `lib/`), keep the schema-validated `bootstrap_armed`/`bootstrap_step` events, and drop the `mp bootstrap` subcommands from the permanent CLI — a design preference, not a correctness defect.

disagreements: Critic-per-round cadence: reviewer 3 rated blocker, reviewer 1 should-fix. Reviewer 3 is right — §4.2 (spec.md:143) claims the cadence is 'enforced, not advisory', §5.3's ask refusal list (spec.md:254) contains no per-round receipt requirement, and §11's test uses the same 'following receipt' predicate, so the planned suite certifies the bypass; this is the rev-13 S6 fix failing on the run's primary goal.

push_archive: reviewer 4 rated blocker, reviewer 1 should-fix (different leg: multi-host non-FF with no recovery). Reviewer 4's severity is supported in-tree — v9 pushes only after the always-halting branch_finish AUQ (lib/finish-step.mjs:316-320, commands/masterplan.md:243,249), every sibling repo on this host with bundles has no `.masterplan.yaml` (so the FF premise fails), §4.1 has no opt-out key, and fleet policy names push a risky-action gate; reviewer 1's non-FF leg is merged as the second failure mode.

Unreviewed local-main commits (step 5): reviewer 1 rated blocker and claimed A21/A28 are false. Downgraded to should-fix: the spec discloses the topology (§10.1.5), the commits are pre-existing repo history that any push would carry, the pre-publish verify covers them functionally, and A21/A28 make no claim about review coverage of that range; the actionable gap is that `publish_ack` does not name them (3 non-bundle commits right now).

deploy_indeterminate 'mark done with evidence': reviewer 1 rated blocker. Should-fix: the path is behind an always-halting AUQ and leaves a durable digest-bearing record, so it is not silent; but it contradicts §7.1's stated invariant and mislabels the archive as `complete`.

commit_paths allowlist: reviewer 1 rated blocker. Nit: the exploit requires the repo author to allowlist `src/` in their own reviewed config or write a version-rewriting step; a seed-time warning and a `${version}` postcondition close it.

Ship-before-review ordering: reviewer 2 (should-fix) wants a different reviewer panel for the pre-publish pass. The operator confirmed the D2/A25 ordering with the S5 mitigation on 2026-09-03 (spec.md:1237, 1298); this is a recorded decision, not a defect — dropped.

Sibling-repo scan: reviewer 4 assumed /srv/workflows is in the step-4 list; reviewer 1 said the scan is not host-wide. Reviewer 1 is right — `<MAIN>/../*` resolves to /srv/dev/ras/*, which contains none of /srv/dev/ehr, /srv/dev/petabit/*, /srv/dev/yanos-project/*, or /srv/workflows; reviewer 4's underlying concern is folded into the scan-coverage should-fix.

Seed-lock race with non-seed writers: reviewer 1 re-raised it; the rev-12 panel dropped the identical claim because §8 discloses the digest as staleness detection and the lock as seed-only. The tree supports the drop again.
dropped: Reviewer 1 should-fix (A29 seed lock vs ordinary plan/goal writers): already disclosed in §8 ('staleness detection, not a lock') and dropped after in-tree verification in the rev-12 panel (gate-spec-panel-3.json); no new evidence.

Reviewer 1 should-fix (A23 critic receipt binds recomputed state, not the dispatched request): §5.3 states the receipt is honesty-bound and 'not tamper-proof and is documented as such'; the rev-11 panel dropped 'receipt provenance strength' on the same ground; a dispatch-request digest would still be orchestrator-supplied.

Reviewer 1 should-fix, attestation half (arm/record never proves the printed command ran): explicitly disclosed as the A33 residual (spec.md:750, 1306) and accepted by the rev-12 panel as the proportionate mitigation; only the failed-record/postcondition ambiguity survives, as a nit.

Reviewer 2 should-fix (A: ship-before-review, demand for a different reviewer panel): the D2/A25 ordering and forward-only recovery are user-confirmed 2026-09-03 with the S5 pre-publish pass as the recorded mitigation; a reviewer-diversity preference, not a defect with a wrong outcome.

Reviewer 2 should-fix (C: split the release into a minimal v10.0 deploy-stage cutover plus v10.1+): scope is user-confirmed (A1–A10, v10.0.0 for the goals-format change); a scoping preference with no concrete wrong outcome beyond generic large-diff risk already mitigated by the pre-publish verify and review.

Reviewer 4 should-fix (hook policy in /srv/workflows mutating during the bootstrap window): premise that /srv/workflows appears in the step-4 scan is wrong (the scan root is /srv/dev/ras/*); the hazard is an operational concurrency concern between two runs the operator drives, not a spec design defect; the actionable coverage gap is kept as the sibling-scan should-fix.

Reviewer 1's sub-claim that A21/A28 are 'false' under the documented topology: neither assumption asserts review coverage of pre-existing local-main history; the substantive gap (commits not named at publish_ack) is kept as a should-fix.
